newsitem.title: USA: NYSE WEEKLY PROGRAM TRADING AVERAGES 15.6 PCT.
newsitem.headline: NYSE WEEKLY PROGRAM TRADING AVERAGES 15.6 PCT.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading averaged 15.6 percent of its average daily volume of 529.9 million shares, or 82.4 million shares, for the week of July 28-August 1.
Program trading accounted for an average of 14.9 percent of average daily volume of 550.6 million shares for the week of July 21-25.
Of the average 582.4 million shares during the week, buy programs accounted for an average 42.3 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 40.1 million daily.
In all markets, program trading averaged 122.6 million shares a day for the week.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, BNP Securities, NatWest, Interactive Brokers and Susquehanna Brokerage Services each executed all of their program activity for customers, as agent.
Morgan Stanely split its program trading activity between its own accounts and thos of its customers.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 78.9 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 19.9 percent of program volume from July 28-August 1.
During the week, 20.1 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 1.1 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
